jobs.title: Clinical Case Manager
jobs.description:

one of the largest and effective nonprofits working to end homelessness in the Bay Area, is seeking a skilled Clinical Case Manager
to help support our Napa County Programs.

The Clinical Case Manager provides clinical case management services to participants and is aimed at increasing wellness, increasing housing stability, and preventing people from cycling through the criminal justice system and/or hospitals. Responsible for needs assessments and delivery of strengths based/needs focused services. Acts as the lead on clinical cases and guides supporting team members in clinical service delivery.

$36.00/hr - $38.00/hr
100% paid medical, dental and vision coverage options for employees
19 days of PTO accrued first year
12 paid holidays/year
403(b) Retirement Plan w/ Employer Match & Contribution Programs

Assist participants with establishing goals and strategies for increasing self-sufficiency.â¯â¯
Coordinate care and discharge planning for participants in institutional settings, hospitals, etc.

This position works closely with medical providers, social workers, case managers, patient navigators, community organizations, health plans, and other stakeholders.

High School Diploma or GED

Experience providing community outreach, education, navigation, or support services

Ability to work independently and collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams

jobs.title: Software Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Efficient Computer is rethinking computing from the ground up to solve one of AI's biggest challenges: energy. Our Fabric architecture delivers a 10–100x improvement in energy efficiency for general-purpose computation, including AI, while supporting familiar programming languages and software frameworks—unlocking new possibilities for autonomous machines, intelligent infrastructure, wearables, and space systems. With our first processor, Electron E1, now shipping in volume and more than $97 million in Series B financing recently announced, we're accelerating customer deployments and scaling our architecture to data center performance. Join us to build the hardware and software that bring intelligence wherever it's needed and help shape the next generation of computing.

Efficient Computer is building the next generation of super-efficient, general-purpose processors around the Fabric architecture, a novel spatial dataflow design. The Fabric is only as useful as the software that targets it: the effcc compiler, the system software stack (optimization libraries such as eff-dsp and, over time, the runtime), and the SDK that customers build on.

We are looking for a Software Technical Program Manager to own the quarterly release of this software, from scoping and commitment through code freeze, qualification, and ship. You will be the operational center of the software program: building and defending the release plan, driving the critical path, holding the quality bar, and making tradeoff conversations happen before something slips. You will work daily with the compiler, system software, embedded, and product teams, and regularly interface with architecture and hardware teams especially when it comes time to bring-up new silicon.

Key Responsibilities

Own the Release

Own the execution of the quarterly software release from planning through ship: the schedule, critical path, and delivery. Product defines what ships and why, Engineering determines what is feasible, and you are accountable for when and how it lands. Each release bundles the SDK, the effcc compiler, optimized software libraries, and eventually the runtime.
Build the release plan with product managers, team leads, and engineering managers. This includes feature commitments, freeze dates, qualification windows, and ship criteria, informed by Product's customer requirements and the hardware schedule.
Drive the weekly execution cadence (release reviews, bug triage, go/no-go) and maintain a single source of truth for status, dependencies, and decisions.

Drive Cross-Functional Execution

Coordinate handoffs across the compiler, system software, and embedded teams, and with architecture, product and hardware teams.
Keep Product Management informed about execution and raise risks accordingly that could affect the release schedule, quality, or feature-set.
Manage the release's dependency chains: e.g. compiler features that libraries depend on, interfaces shared between the SDK and the runtime, LLVM and toolchain versions, board and silicon availability, etc.

Maintain Release Quality

Establish with our teams release quality gates: e.g. no regressions in cycles, energy, or code size on the benchmark suites relative to the previous release; test coverage thresholds met, etc.

Run the release checklist (the gates above plus documentation, release notes, etc.), working with the release shepherd to hold owners to closure criteria.

Track escaped defects and feed what we learn back into the checklist.

Manage Risk, Decisions, and Reporting

Surface risk early with mitigation options and schedule impact quantified: e.g. late compiler features, coverage shortfalls, and benchmark regressions.
Facilitate scope, schedule, and quality tradeoffs, and document what was decided, by whom, and why.
Deliver executive reporting: where the release stands, what is at risk, what decision is needed and by when.

Required Qualifications

B.S. in Electrical/Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent; M.S. or MBA a plus.
7+ years in software engineering or program management, including prior hands-on engineering experience in compilers, systems software, or embedded software.
Working fluency in using AI-tools to facilitate program management – from reporting, to issue tracking, to dependency analysis and more.
Strong experience with the software delivery flow: compiler toolchains, embedded SDKs, CI/CD, test coverage, performance benchmarking, and release engineering.
Demonstrated ability to build and defend a bottoms-up schedule with critical path analysis and dependency mapping.
Track record influencing without authority: earning the technical credibility to push senior engineers on commitments and dates.
Strong written and verbal communication; able to run a room of principal engineers and an executive review with equal effectiveness.
Hands-on with program tooling: Github, Linear, Jira, Notion, Confluence, CI systems, etc.

Desired Qualifications & Experience Requirements

Experience as the technical program manager on a first-generation silicon product, where the toolchain and hardware matured together.
Familiarity with LLVM or MLIR, machine learning compilers, or language runtimes.
Knowledge of dataflow, spatial, or other novel compute architectures.
Experience managing pre-silicon software enablement against emulation or FPGA prototyping programs.

We offer a competitive base salary for this role, generally ranging from $200,000 to $260,000, plus a 10% annual bonus, meaningful equity, and comprehensive benefits. Final compensation will depend on experience, level, and location, with flexibility for the right candidate.

Why Join Efficient?

Build what's next. At Efficient, you'll tackle big challenges with room to take ownership and make an impact. We back you with competitive pay, equity, a 401(k) match, company-paid benefits, paid parental leave, and flexibility—plus opportunities to grow your skills and career as we scale.

jobs.description:
Everpure (NYSE: P) has evolved from storage pioneer to data platform, closing fiscal 2026 with $3.7 billion in revenue, its first billion-dollar quarter, and accelerating growth into FY27. Our strategic agenda spans the companies defining the next era of technology - hyperscalers, AI labs, the AI hardware supply chain, data platform providers, and the broader AI ecosystem.

This type of work—work that changes the world—is what the tech industry was founded on. So, if you're ready to seize the endless opportunities and leave your mark, come join us.

THE ROLE

Everpure's global contract manufacturing network needs a single owner for capacity governance and supply chain network resilience — someone who replaces fragmented, reactive decision-making with one coherent framework spanning all lines of business. This role sits at the center of that shift: building the governance structures, risk frameworks, and executive reporting that let the network absorb shocks — geopolitical, infrastructure, business continuity — without derailing growth targets. You'll work closely with the Network Design Council, site managers, CM partners, and cross-functional teams like Mfg Product & Test Engineering, R&D Engineering, and Indirect Sourcing, with real influence over how capacity and risk decisions get made across the network.

What You'll Do

Own and govern the Global Capacity Planning Framework, building the RACI that gives the Supply Chain Network Council one source of truth across all lines of business
Serve as the central escalation point for capacity issues network-wide, running a Monthly Global Capacity Review and standardized dashboards that keep site managers and CM partners aligned
Define and govern Time to Recover (TTR) and Time to Survive/Time to Fail (TTF) resilience KPIs across all global production sites and products, translating gaps into prioritized mitigation plans for the highest-risk sites
Drive the Capacity Analysis Tool and executive Tableau dashboard roadmap, and own the capital budget that funds capacity and resilience investments against growth targets
Partner with Indirect Sourcing and Engineering to optimize test process & time, landed cost through data research, common infrastructure parts and improved CM pricing and forecasting

What You Bring

Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Hardware Engineering, Operations Research, Supply Chain, or related field; Master’s degree preferred. Six Sigma Green Belt certification or above preferred.
An industrial process engineering mindset — comfortable applying process analysis, simulation, optimization/heuristics, or forecasting to translate operational data (cost, service, capability, emissions) into network design decisions.
Proven ability to lead complex, technically-oriented transformation projects, utilizing methodologies like Waterfall, Agile, or Scrum to manage scope, schedules, and deliverables in a dynamic environment, paired with exceptional communication and negotiation skills to translate technical/data concepts for non-technical stakeholders and build consensus across supply chain, IT, and engineering teams.
Deep fluency in global contract manufacturing capacity planning, built through experience designing governance frameworks, RACIs, and executive review cadences that hold up across a complex, matrixed network
Strong analytical capability — comfortable building capacity models and KPI dashboards in tools like Tableau, and partnering with BI/analytics teams on executive-facing reporting
Experience building supply chain risk and resilience programs, including business continuity planning, scenario analysis, and recovery metrics such as Time to Recover and Time to Survive/Fail
Skilled at driving alignment across cross-functional, matrixed teams without direct authority — able to influence site managers, CM partners, and senior stakeholders toward a shared framework
We are primarily an in-office environment and therefore, you will be expected to work from the Santa Clara, CA office in compliance with Everpure's policies, unless you are on PTO, or work travel, or other approved leave.

Salary ranges are determined based on role, level and location. For positions open to candidates in multiple geographical locations, the base salary range is reflective of the labor market across the applicable locations.

This role may be eligible for incentive pay and/or equity.

There is no application deadline and we accept applications on an ongoing basis until the job is filled.

$153,000—$230,000 USD

Innovation: We celebrate those who think critically, like a challenge, and aspire to be trailblazers.
Growth: We give you the space and support to grow along with us and to contribute to something meaningful. We have been named Fortune's Best Workplaces in Technology™, Fortune's Best Workplaces in the Bay Area™, and certified as a Great Place to Work®!
Team: We build each other up and set aside ego for the greater good.

And because we understand the value of bringing your full and best self to work, we offer a variety of perks to manage a healthy balance, including flexible time off, wellness resources, and company-sponsored team events. Check out http://benefits.everpuredata.com/ for more information.

Accommodations And Accessibility

Our Commitment To a Strong And Inclusive Team

We’re forging a future where everyone finds their rightful place and where every voice matters. Where uniqueness isn’t just accepted but embraced. That’s why we are committed to fostering the growth and development of every person, cultivating a sense of community through our Employee Resource Groups and advocating for inclusive leadership.

jobs.title: Embedded Program Manager
jobs.description:
Description

Northland Controls is seeking an experienced Embedded Program Manager in Sunnyvale, CA. This is an exciting opportunity for a proven security industry professional who enjoys working closely with enterprise customers, leading global service programs, developing high-performing teams, and continuously improving service delivery.

In this role, you will be embedded within a key enterprise customer account, serving as a trusted program partner and primary point of coordination between the customer and Northland Controls. You will lead a multidisciplinary embedded team that may include Project Managers, consultants, systems technicians, and engineers, ensuring services are delivered in accordance with program requirements and customer priorities.

You will maintain regular touch points with the global team, review and verify work, provide monthly program updates, partner with customer leadership on challenges and opportunities, and lead quarterly business reviews focused on KPIs, SLAs, priorities, and continuous improvement. You will also be accountable for the performance and development of each team member and for making resource or team adjustments when delivery expectations are not being met.

If you're looking for an opportunity to become deeply integrated with a global customer program, strengthen service delivery, develop talented teams, and make a measurable impact in a growing organization, we'd love to hear from you.

What You'll Do

Serve as the embedded program leader within a key enterprise customer account, developing a strong understanding of the customer's organization, security program, priorities, standards, operating model, and long-term objectives.
Maintain daily or regular touch points with the global embedded team to review priorities, verify work, remove blockers, and ensure services are being delivered in accordance with program requirements.
Act as the primary point of contact between the customer and Northland Controls for program-level planning, performance, communication, escalation, and issue resolution.
Partner closely with customer management on strategic focus areas, active projects, delivery improvements, program challenges, opportunities, and the ongoing evolution of the program.
Lead, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary team that may include Project Managers, consultants, systems technicians, and engineers, fostering a collaborative and high-performing work environment.
Establish clear expectations for each team member and hold individuals accountable for performance, service quality, responsiveness, and delivery commitments.
Provide ongoing coaching, feedback, mentorship, and direction; manage performance improvement and corrective action in accordance with Northland processes, and recommend team adjustments when sustained improvement is not achieved.
Allocate and prioritize resources across projects, operational needs, and customer initiatives while balancing workloads and optimizing utilization, productivity, and coverage.
Track program performance using KPIs, SLAs, delivery milestones, workload data, and other relevant metrics; identify trends and take action when performance is at risk.
Prepare and deliver regular program updates to customer stakeholders and Northland leadership, including performance, resource, financial, risk, and improvement reporting.
Lead the development and presentation of Quarterly Business Reviews, coordinating team inputs, reporting against KPIs and SLAs, collecting customer feedback, aligning on quarterly priorities, and driving follow-through on agreed actions.
Build and maintain trusted relationships with customer stakeholders, proactively managing expectations, addressing concerns, and supporting strong satisfaction and confidence in the team's services.
Track and analyze relationship and service indicators, including stakeholder feedback, responsiveness, recurring concerns, and service-quality trends, to assess the effectiveness of program delivery and relationship management.
Identify program risks, dependencies, and issues; develop mitigation plans and work with customer management and Northland leadership to proactively address challenges and keep delivery on track.
Manage the overall embedded team budget, monitor expenditures and forecasts, identify budget risks, and provide monthly financial and accrual reporting as required.
Conduct regular quality reviews of team outputs and service delivery to ensure work aligns with customer requirements, established standards, and program expectations.
Drive continuous improvement by analyzing scheduling, workload, performance, and service data to identify inefficiencies, bottlenecks, and opportunities to improve delivery processes and outcomes.
Coordinate across internal teams, customer stakeholders, program peers, suppliers, and dependency partners to align delivery, share best practices, and ensure seamless integration of work across the program.
Gather and analyze feedback from customer stakeholders and team members and translate that feedback into practical improvements to services, processes, team performance, and working relationships.
Proactively identify and resolve conflicts, facilitating practical solutions and timely escalation when issues require additional leadership involvement.
Conduct periodic program evaluations and lessons-learned reviews to assess outcomes, document improvements, and inform future program planning and service strategy.
Travel to customer locations and team sites as required.

What We're Looking For

Significant experience managing complex enterprise programs, embedded services, or technical service-delivery teams within the security industry or a closely related technical environment.
Proven experience working directly with enterprise customers and managing long-term customer relationships in a high-visibility, service-oriented environment.
Proven experience leading, coaching, and developing multidisciplinary teams, including direct accountability for individual performance and service delivery.
Strong experience with KPI and SLA management, executive-level program reporting, Quarterly Business Reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Strong understanding of program financial management, budgeting, forecasting, accrual reporting, resource planning, workload balancing, and cost controls.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, stakeholders, dependencies, and competing requirements within a large global customer environment.
Strong knowledge of physical security systems and services, including access control, video surveillance, and related enterprise technologies.
Experience with Lenel, Software House, or similar enterprise security platforms; relevant certifications are highly desirable.
PMP certification or equivalent program or project management credentials preferred.
Excellent leadership, communication, presentation, facilitation, and organizational skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with both technical teams and senior customer stakeholders.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify trends, anticipate risks, navigate changing priorities, and drive issues through resolution.
Ability to build productive, trusted relationships with customers, colleagues, suppliers, and business partners while operating effectively as both a customer-facing partner and a representative of Northland Controls.
Valid driver's license and ability to travel as required.

Why Join Northland Controls?

At Northland Controls, you'll have the opportunity to become an integral part of a key enterprise customer's global security program while leading the people, processes, and performance that support consistent service delivery. You'll work alongside experienced customer, project, engineering, and operations professionals while helping strengthen the teams and operating practices that support our continued growth.

We value innovation, accountability, collaboration, and doing what it takes to deliver exceptional results for our customers. As an Embedded Program Manager, you'll have the opportunity to build lasting customer partnerships, develop your team, improve how services are delivered, and make a meaningful impact across the organization.

Northland Controls offers competitive compensation, comprehensive health and retirement benefits, professional development opportunities, and a flexible working environment.

jobs.title: Community Health Worker
jobs.description:
Company Description

At Henry Ford Health, we're committed to advancing health and improving lives for the millions of people we serve across Michigan and around the world. As one of the nation's leading academic health systems, we provide a comprehensive continuum of care that includes primary and preventive services, specialty and complex care, virtual care, pharmacy, home health, eye care, health insurance, and more. With 12 hospitals and hundreds of ambulatory care locations, including former Ascension Southeast Michigan and Flint Region facilities, our growing network expands access to exceptional care in the communities we serve.

Headquartered in Detroit, Henry Ford Health is helping shape the future of healthcare through the transformative Future of Health: Detroit initiative, a $3 billion investment that is redefining our academic healthcare campus and advancing innovation, research, education, and community impact.

Our work is grounded in purpose, collaboration, and belonging. We empower team members to grow their careers, contribute innovative ideas, and make a meaningful difference every day. Whether you're caring for patients, supporting operations, conducting research, or driving new solutions, you'll be part of a team united by a shared mission: delivering exceptional care, advancing health outcomes, and building healthier communities for all.

Job Description

GENERAL SUMMARY:

As a Community Health Worker (CHW), you'll be a trusted bridge between healthcare, social services, and the communities we serve—making a real difference in people's lives every day. Under the leadership of the Office of Community Health, Equity & Wellness' CHW Hub Manager, and in partnership with designated onsite leaders, you'll serve as a vital liaison who promotes access to healthcare services, improves health and equity outcomes, and helps patients navigate the systems that support their wellbeing. Whether integrated directly within a clinical care team or assigned to a specific project, you'll play a critical role in addressing social determinants of health (SDOH), connecting individuals to essential services, and delivering patient-centered, culturally relevant care that truly matters.

Principal Duties And Responsibilities

Identify and address patients' non-medical and social determinant of health needs—including food security, housing, transportation, and social support—by providing meaningful referrals to appropriate social service agencies and tracking positive outcomes.
Collaborate with clinical care teams to ensure seamless continuity of care, co-develop personalized care plans, and provide compassionate follow-up support through home visits and telephonic check-ins that strengthen patient relationships.
Drive patient engagement and retention by conducting direct outreach that improves recruitment, supports adherence to care instructions, and increases utilization of primary and preventive care services—ultimately reducing no-show rates and unnecessary emergency department visits.
Build trust and foster community connections through authentic outreach that helps bridge healthcare services with the communities we serve.
Empower patients through culturally competent health education and coaching—delivered individually and in group settings—that focuses on disease prevention, health promotion, and effective chronic disease management.
Advocate for patients by identifying and removing barriers to care (such as insurance enrollment, transportation, housing, and language access), facilitating connections to resources, and supporting individuals in confidently navigating both healthcare and social service systems.
Promote health literacy and patient self-advocacy by providing guidance on self-management of chronic conditions, system navigation, and personal empowerment strategies.
Maintain accurate, timely documentation of patient encounters and contribute to the evaluation of community and population health initiatives by collecting and analyzing relevant data within Henry Ford's electronic health record and other prescribed documentation tools.
Connect patients with HFH classes, support groups, and related services, assisting with recruitment and enrollment to expand access to care resources.
Continuously expand your knowledge and expertise through ongoing training, staying current with community resources, prescribed curriculums, IRB protocols, and organizational policies relevant to your caseload or project.

Qualifications

EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE REQUIRED:

High school diploma or G.E.D. equivalent.
Previous experience as a community health worker, preferred.
Previous experience conducting health education, or working with underserved populations, preferred.
Previous experience conducting home and/or clinic visits with patients and their primary care providers, preferred.

Additional Information

CERTIFICATIONS/LICENSURES REQUIRED:

Certification as a Community Health Worker or a willingness to become certified within six months of hire.

Skills & Competencies

Ability to build trust with the community and maintain ethical standards of care.
Knowledge of local health resources and the social service system.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to work with diverse communities.
Cultural competency, particularly with underserved or marginalized populations.
Must meet or exceed core customer service responsibilities, standards and behaviors as outlined in the Henry Ford Health Customer Service Policy
Must practice the customer skills as provided through on-going training and in-services.

Physical Demands/Working Conditions

Depending on the specific needs of assigned work, there may be variations of inperson, hybrid or remote office-based work with frequent community outreach, including home visits and attendance at community events. Must have a valid State of Michigan driver’s license and automobile insurance.

GENERAL SUMMARY:

The Community Health Worker (CHW) for the WIN Network primarily co-facilitates Group Prenatal Care (GPC) sessions, ensuring effective coordination, logistics, and participant engagement. The role includes identifying patients with clinical risk factors and facilitating appropriate referrals and follow-up care. CHWs provide targeted health education and coaching on prenatal care and healthy behaviors, conduct Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) screenings to identify and address barriers to care, and connect patients to community resources to support service utilization. Additionally, the CHW supports care coordination by serving as a liaison between patients and the clinical care team, promoting engagement and adherence to care plans.

Principle Duties And Responsibilities

Co-facilitates Group Prenatal Care (GPC) sessions by coordinating activities, managing logistics, scheduling guest speakers, and ensuring a structured, welcoming environment for participants.

Conducts Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) screenings to identify barriers to care, including housing, food insecurity, and transportation, and supports integration into care plans.
Coordinates connections to community-based resources, ensuring patients receive appropriate referrals and follow-up to promote service utilization.
Serves as a liaison between patients and the clinical care team, supporting care coordination, reinforcing treatment plans, and promoting patient engagement and adherence.

Ability to build trust with the community and maintain ethical standards of care.

who demonstrates this mission and wants to work for an organization that makes a difference in the community.

What you will be doing?

Care Coordination and Support: Intensive Care Coordination (CCSI)
. CCSI is provided to children stratified into Tier 2. Designated CCSI Care Coordinators work with an average of 16 families at a time and are never assigned to work with more than 18 families at once.

Care Coordination And Support (CCS) Is The Foundational Service That Care Coordination And Support Organizations Provide To Pathways Enrolled Children And Families. Coordinating and consulting with MCOs, providers, other child-serving systems, and any other support involved with the child’s care. This includes helping transition children from an institutional setting, including from an out-of-state setting to a community-based living arrangement; and,
Referring, linking, and following-up with service providers and social service agencies for services recommended by the CFT on the service plan.
Documentation of Pathways Program activities, and services provided.

Monitors and updates information regarding insurance data, authorizations, preferred providers and changes in patient’s treatment plan. Partners with the clinical care team and insurance provider to ensure continued coverage of patient’s care and maximum reimbursement and minimized financial impact to the patient.
Provides administrative support in maintaining materials such as documents, proposals, routine correspondence, spreadsheets, composing and preparing routine reports, and maintaining records in a variety of business software and database applications for electronic medical records, billing, data management.

Optimizes patient experience by using effective customer service. Uses discretion and is attentive to issues of customer confidentiality. Demonstrates skills in pro-active resolution and attempts to resolve scheduling conflicts.
May manage the medical record for the assigned area, including coordination with hospitals, practice offices and other ancillary services to obtain needed records. Responds to patient referral requests for tests, procedures and specialty visits. Follows guidelines and may assist in developing procedures to ensure that medical records are in compliance with all state and federal laws. May also reconcile charge tickets, identifying incomplete tickets, missing charge codes or missing diagnosis codes. Notifies clinical staff as needed.
Works independently under general supervision, following established procedures. Uses knowledge and problem-solving skills to work independently in a clinic/physician practice environment. Responsibility for ensuring efficient coordination of administrative functions supporting patient needs assessments, insurance and authorization verification, registration, maintaining and handling of documentation, financial counseling, and scheduling of appointments. Internal and external customers include patients and their families, physician offices, third party payors, vendors, clinical staff, ancillary staff, therapist, nurses and case managers. Primary responsibility is to main department assigned, however cross-over and assistance to other departments is required.

High school diploma/GED or equivalent working knowledge.

Requires skills and abilities typically attained with three or more years working in a hospital or medical office. Requires knowledge of medical terminology. Job Summary

This position is eligible for a $2500 retention bonus.

The Providence Center Residential Case Manager Women's Road to Recovery provides clinical case management services to support and advance program goals and objectives through a high-quality, client-centered approach. They identify clients’ needs using a person-centered framework that addresses mental health symptoms as well as co-occurring disorders. They also collaborate with clients to achieve the highest possible level of independence.

Duties & Responsibilities

Coordinate and deliver person-centered, recovery-oriented case management as part of a multidisciplinary team.
Work closely with the care team to align case management services with clients’ mental health treatment plans.
Conduct comprehensive assessments to identify client needs related to housing, education, employment, financial stability, healthcare, and community resources.
Develop, present and implement individualized care plans in collaboration with the care team, clients and their families as appropriate.
Provide support counseling with mental health issues, substance use disorders, and medical conditions.
Provide ongoing monitoring and follow-up to ensure client needs are met and progress is achieved. Implement emergency protocols when required.
Assist clients with daily activities and life skills through modeling and providing education to promote independence. This includes medication management and budgeting as appropriate.
Supervise clients self-administering medications while using the 6 Rights of Medication Self-Administration.
Assist and monitor the group home clients with medical interventions and hygiene needs.
Conduct daily room/unit inspections.
Provide and maintain a home atmosphere.
Assist in the development and implementation of socialization and recreational activities within the group home, in the community, and by attending Day Program groups and activities.
Negotiate and schedule appointments for clients within The Center and with community partners (Social Security Supplemental Insurance (S.S.I.), SNAP, Advocates Office, Medical Doctor, etc.).
Connect clients to community resources, including social services, transportation, and financial assistance programs.
Serve as a liaison between clients and community agencies, advocating for client needs and facilitating access to services.
Maintain and promote family contacts and relationships.
Provide education and guidance to clients and families on navigating systems such as healthcare, education, and social services.
Identify, assess and respond to clinical emergencies and crisis situations, including suicide risk and danger to others. Perform crisis intervention and risk management as needed, escalating to appropriate resources when indicated (Qualified Mental Health Professionals/QMHPs or Emergency Services).
Maintain accurate, detailed, and timely records of all client interactions and services provided, including clinical documentation as required.
Prepare reports and documentation as required for audits and program evaluation.
Ensure compliance with agency policies, ethical standards, and regulatory requirements.
Attend team meetings and case reviews to share updates and collaboratively address client challenges.
Develop professional relationships with Day Program staff.
Foster cooperative relationships with staff, clients, and community partners.
Transport clients safely to appointments and activities as needed.
Enter Work Request Orders for facility-related issues as needed and communicate such to department team.
Attend trainings and case presentations.
Serve on committees and participate in agency initiatives as assigned.
Perform other duties as assigned to support client goals and program needs.

Requirements

High School or GED Required.
Minimum 1 to 3 Years of experience in a behavioral health setting. Experience in residential facilities preferred.
Must have valid driver's license, registration, current inspection and insured automobile.
Strong knowledge of community resources and systems, including housing, education, employment, and healthcare.
Ability to build rapport and establish trust with diverse clients and community partners.
Cultural competence and commitment to providing equitable and inclusive services.
Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, to convey information clearly and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams.
Excellent organizational, problem-solving, and time management skills.
Proficiency in documentation and electronic record-keeping systems, including ability to document in electronic medical records.
Ability to travel within the community with reliable transportation.
Able to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, holidays and during inclement weather, as well as cover the program when unforeseen circumstances arise to ensure 24-hour coverage. Work environment is a residential setting for adults with severe psychiatric illness that require 24/7 monitoring.
Bilingual preferred. For positions designated as bilingual (Bil), proficiency in the required language is mandatory, and the language assessment must be passed no later than 30 days of starting the role.

Care New England Health System (CNE)
and its member institutions, Butler Hospital, Women & Infants Hospital, Kent Hospital, VNA of Care New England, Integra, The Providence Center, and Care New England Medical Group, is a trusted, integrated health care organization that fuels the latest advances in medical research, attracts the nation’s top specialty-trained doctors, hones renowned services and innovative programs, and engages in the important discussions people need to have about their health and end-of-life wishes. Overview

The Mayor’s Office of Housing (MOH) works to foster healthy, vibrant, and welcoming communities for all by ensuring stable, green, and accessible housing and the sustainable use of land. MOH oversees programs that create and preserve affordable housing, support homeowners and renters, provide housing and services to individuals and families experiencing homelessness, and develop city-owned property. MOH envisions a Boston where all residents have the homes and neighborhoods they need to thrive.

Within MOH, the Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing Program engages with real estate developers, marketing agents, property managers, and the public to foster fair housing practices and ensure equitable access to affordable housing opportunities in Boston.

Under the supervision of the Affirmative Marketing Senior Program Manager, the Program Manager helps develop and maintain systems and resources for accessing and maintaining income-restricted housing with a critical eye toward equity, transparency, and accountability. The Program Manager provides technical assistance and guidance to property owners and their agents, City housing development officers and project managers, and other stakeholders related to income-restricted housing development. The Program Manager performs this function to ensure that the program effectively engages and serves residents, especially the most vulnerable, to achieve the program’s mission.

Maintains and develops project auditing systems designed to keep projects on track and in compliance with fair housing contracts.
Develops and maintains Affirmative Marketing Plan Guidance to ensure and expand access to the public.
Contributes to research and development of resources that make accessing and maintaining affordable housing more transparent.
Conducts Affirmative Marketing workshops and presentations for City agencies, developers, and other external agencies and ensures accessibility to the public.
Collaborates with representatives of City agencies or departments in efforts to expand access to income-restricted housing opportunities.

Prepares reports of findings as necessary and maintains program files.

jobs.description:

Department: Environmental and Occupational Health

Job Title: Professional Research Assistant Level 2

Position #:00853624 – Requisition #: 41280

Job Summary:

The Center for Health, Work, and Environment (CHWE) is seeking a part-time (50%FTE) Professional Research Assistant (PRA) – Level 2 position. This position will serve as an essential liaison and trusted bridge between the Mountain West Hub research team and local residents in Alamosa, CO. As part of a landmark clean air and health resilience study, the PRA is responsible for conducting community-based recruitment, securing informed consent, conducting structured home visits, placing indoor air filtration units, and collecting longitudinal health and environmental metrics across participating households.

Community Outreach & Recruitment

Local Outreach & Engagement: Conduct direct outreach across Alamosa County to engage residents in the Clean Air Study. Represent the study at community meetings, local events, and public hubs to build awareness and trust.
Participant Recruitment Waves: Reach out to households identified through randomized address sampling and community sign-up lists, maintaining respectful, multi-modal contact attempts (phone, in-person, email).
Recruitment Tracking: Maintain accurate, real-time records of all participant contact attempts, eligibility screenings, and recruitment dispositions using REDCap and shared tracking logs.

Informed Consent & Participant Onboarding

Study Explanation & Screening: Clearly explain study objectives, household eligibility criteria (year-round SLV residence, no existing air cleaner, adult 18+ household consent), and participation benefits ($200 incentive + free air filter).
Consent Administration: Guide participants through the informed consent process (via phone, Zoom link, or in person) and collect child assents during initial visits in accordance with IRB protocols.

Home Visits & Environmental / Health Data Collection

In-Home Monitoring & Equipment Setup: Perform initial, quarterly/midpoint, and endpoint home visits to measure indoor air quality, record room dimensions, and set up DIY box-fan air cleaners (DIYacs) and UPAS air quality monitors.
Health Measurement Collection: Collect baseline and follow-up clinical and survey measures, including resting blood pressure, lung function testing (spirometry/PEF), survey responses, and urine sample coordination for designated sub-cohorts.
Equipment Maintenance & Inspection: Inspect air filter units and sensors during routine visits, ensuring proper placement in participant bedrooms or primary living areas and supplying replacement filters as needed.

Acute Air Quality Event & Longitudinal Support

Poor Air Quality Event Follow-Up: Assist participants during text-alerted poor air quality events (wildfire smoke or dust events) by supporting short 3-day daily surveys and lung function measurements.
Ongoing Participant Support: Serve as the primary local point of contact for participating Alamosa households, delivering plain-language air quality/health results summaries and addressing participant questions.

Training, Logistics & Compliance

Required Study Trainings: Complete mandatory pre-study onboarding, including CITI Human Subjects Training, REDCap data collection training, recruitment protocol review, and the 8-hour Full Study Training.
Team Meetings & Administrative Reporting: Participate in bi-weekly (and subsequent monthly) study team check-ins, coordinate with local couriers for sample/hardware handoffs, and submit monthly invoices and mileage logs to the CN Manager.

Work Location:

Remote – this role is eligible to work remotely, but the employee must be in the United States.

Why Join Us:

The Colorado School of Public Health is a collaborative endeavor involving the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus (CU Anschutz), Colorado State University (CSU), and the University of Northern Colorado (UNC). The Colorado School of Public Health is the first and only accredited school of public health in the Rocky Mountain Region, attracting top-tier faculty and students from across the country and providing vital contributions towards ensuring our region’s health and well-being. Collaboratively formed in 2008 by CU Anschutz, CSU, and UNC, the Colorado School of Public Health provides education programs, including a Master’s concentration in global health, innovative research that places the School in the top 20 in NIH funding among Schools of Public Health, and community service that addresses public health issues including chronic disease, healthcare access, climate, and environmental threats, emerging infectious diseases, population mental health, ONE HEALTH and injuries for the Rocky Mountain region, nationally and globally.

Why work for the University?

We have AMAZING benefits and offer exceptional amounts of holiday, vacation and sick leave! The University of Colorado offers an excellent benefits package including:

Medical: Multiple plan options
Dental: Multiple plan options
Additional Insurance: Disability, Life, Vision
Retirement 401(a) Plan: Employer contributes 10% of your gross pay
Paid Time Off: Accruals over the year (based on percentage of time)
Vacation Days: 22/year (maximum accrual 352 hours)
Sick Days: 15/year (unlimited maximum accrual)
Holiday Days: 11/year
Tuition Benefit: Employees have access to this benefit on all CU campuses
ECO Pass: Reduced rate RTD Bus and light rail service

There are many additional perks & programs with the CU Advantage.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

Applicants must meet minimum qualifications at the time of hire.

Must have Bachelor’s degree and 1+ year experience, community health, research coordination, or public service outreach, preferably in rural health initiatives
Bilingual in English and Spanish
Basic computer and mobile technology literacy (e.g., using smartphones, tablets, Zoom, Google Sheets, and web-based survey software like REDCap).
Interpersonal and Communication Skills

Conditions of Employment

Must be available to work year-round in Alamosa, CO, and have the ability to travel for local home visits across Alamosa County. Flexible work schedule requiring some evening and weekend hours to accommodate participant home visit availability.

Preferred Qualifications:

Community Health / Outreach Experience: Prior experience working as a Community Health Worker (CHW), Promotora, patient navigator, research assistant, or community outreach worker in rural health or environmental health programs.
Established Local Networks: Established relationships with local community organizations, clinics, schools, agricultural groups, or public hubs in Alamosa and the San Luis Valley.
Field Data Collection Experience: Prior experience conducting structured home visits, administering surveys, or collecting basic health measurements (e.g., resting blood pressure or peak flow lung function)

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

Community Dynamics: Deep familiarity with local geography, rural cultural norms, and community resources in Alamosa County and surrounding Valley communities.
Interpersonal & Cultural Responsiveness: Strong active listening and trust-building skills; ability to communicate warmly and respectfully with varied rural populations.
Technical & Equipment Handling: Practical aptitude to set up, demonstrate, and inspect household air cleaning hardware (DIY box-fan air cleaners / DIYacs) and air quality monitoring devices (UPAS units).
Digital & Survey Literacy: Proficiency in using smartphones, tablets, or computers for field data collection, including entering survey responses into REDCap, updating Google Sheets tracking logs, and participating in Zoom team check-ins.

The City of Sioux Falls Health Department is accepting applications for a part-time Community Health Worker at Falls Community Health. This position is a maximum of 28 hours per week, M-F, with flexible schedule based on the needs of the clinic.

Community Health Workers work in clinical, community-based and home settings to provide care coordination and connection to resources and support to patients to improve their health and general well-being through education and coordinated care and services.

Responsibilities Included In This Position Are As Follows

Provide community- and clinic-based HIV testing and counseling.
Provide PrEP education and navigation, including helping individuals understand PrEP.
Educate community members about HIV prevention, PrEP, routine HIV testing, and the importance of knowing your HIV status.
Participate in community outreach events, health fairs, testing events, and other HIV prevention activities.

Build relationships with community organizations and other partners to expand awareness of and access to HIV prevention services.

Engage individuals who may not routinely access traditional healthcare settings and connect them with appropriate testing, prevention, and care resources.

Graduation from high school or GED certification with one (1) year experience in a clinical or social services setting; or any such combination of education, experience, and training as may be acceptable to the hiring authority.

This position for the College of Allied Health Sciences (CAHS) plays a pivotal leadership role in the administration and strategic direction of undergraduate academic programs, with a significant emphasis on managing academic and accreditation activities. This multifaceted position demands a high degree of autonomy and expertise in managing various critical aspects of program development and oversight.

This position will be in support of Uniformed Services University, Southern Campus, College of Allied Health Sciences (CAHS), located in San Antonio, Texas.

The Henry M. Jackson Foundation for the Advancement of Military Medicine (HJF) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing military medicine. We serve military, medical, academic and government clients by administering, managing and supporting preeminent scientific programs that benefit members of the armed forces and civilians alike. Since its founding in 1983, HJF has served as a vital link between the military medical community and its federal and private partners. HJF's support and administrative capabilities allow military medical researchers and clinicians to maintain their scientific focus and accomplish their research goals.

Responsibilities

Strategic development, meticulous management, and effective implementation of undergraduate curricula within allied. Collaborate with internal and external academic partners, faculty members across various disciplines.
Responsibility to plan/forecast, prepare, approve, and monitor budgets and identifies a budget range of $500,000-$1,500,000.

Oversee a collection of related/integrated projects that together support a long-term research initiative. Manage key program elements. Oversee the evaluation of academic operations and programs.
Identify project interdependencies, aligning resources and efforts where appropriate. Collect and analyze data on program effectiveness to make datadriven decisions and reports findings to leadership. Lead the design, implementation, and evaluation of new educational programs and initiatives.
Actively contributes to the strategic planning process for the CAHS. Minimum of 6 - 8 years experience required.

In-depth knowledge of federal budget processes and fundamental principles of project management.
Solid Interpersonal skills, including the ability to clearly communicate verbally and in writing, build and maintain teams, and identify and resolve problems.
Demonstrated ability to plan, schedule, and coordinate activities to meet deadlines.
Working knowledge of a variety of software including but not limited to Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, proposal/project tracking, and data analysis software.
Prior experience in the Department of Defense, Military Health System as a Senior Advisor strongly preferred.
Manage the review, development, and approval of undergraduate degree plans, ensuring accuracy and compliance with university policies and procedures. This includes collaborating with academic advisors and program directors to ensure student success.
Ability to obtain and maintain a T1/Public Trust background check.

Military clinical background (preferred). Military Instructor Certification from the branch(s) of Service where experience was gained.

This position will take place primarily in an office setting.

Company Description

At Henry Ford Health, we're committed to advancing health and improving lives for the millions of people we serve across Michigan and around the world. As one of the nation's leading academic health systems, we provide a comprehensive continuum of care that includes primary and preventive services, specialty and complex care, virtual care, pharmacy, home health, eye care, health insurance, and more. With 12 hospitals and hundreds of ambulatory care locations, including former Ascension Southeast Michigan and Flint Region facilities, our growing network expands access to exceptional care in the communities we serve.

Headquartered in Detroit, Henry Ford Health is helping shape the future of healthcare through the transformative Future of Health: Detroit initiative, a $3 billion investment that is redefining our academic healthcare campus and advancing innovation, research, education, and community impact.

Our work is grounded in purpose, collaboration, and belonging. We empower team members to grow their careers, contribute innovative ideas, and make a meaningful difference every day. new_jobs.title: Software Technical Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Efficient Computer is rethinking computing from the ground up to solve one of AI's biggest challenges: energy. Our Fabric architecture delivers a 10–100x improvement in energy efficiency for general-purpose computation, including AI, while supporting familiar programming languages and software frameworks—unlocking new possibilities for autonomous machines, intelligent infrastructure, wearables, and space systems. With our first processor, Electron E1, now shipping in volume and more than $97 million in Series B financing recently announced, we're accelerating customer deployments and scaling our architecture to data center performance. Join us to build the hardware and software that bring intelligence wherever it's needed and help shape the next generation of computing.

Efficient Computer is building the next generation of super-efficient, general-purpose processors around the Fabric architecture, a novel spatial dataflow design. The Fabric is only as useful as the software that targets it: the effcc compiler, the system software stack (optimization libraries such as eff-dsp and, over time, the runtime), and the SDK that customers build on.

We are looking for a Software Technical Program Manager to own the quarterly release of this software, from scoping and commitment through code freeze, qualification, and ship. You will be the operational center of the software program: building and defending the release plan, driving the critical path, holding the quality bar, and making tradeoff conversations happen before something slips. You will work daily with the compiler, system software, embedded, and product teams, and regularly interface with architecture and hardware teams especially when it comes time to bring-up new silicon.

Key Responsibilities

Own the Release

Own the execution of the quarterly software release from planning through ship: the schedule, critical path, and delivery. Product defines what ships and why, Engineering determines what is feasible, and you are accountable for when and how it lands. Each release bundles the SDK, the effcc compiler, optimized software libraries, and eventually the runtime.
Build the release plan with product managers, team leads, and engineering managers. This includes feature commitments, freeze dates, qualification windows, and ship criteria, informed by Product's customer requirements and the hardware schedule.
Drive the weekly execution cadence (release reviews, bug triage, go/no-go) and maintain a single source of truth for status, dependencies, and decisions.

Drive Cross-Functional Execution

Coordinate handoffs across the compiler, system software, and embedded teams, and with architecture, product and hardware teams.
Keep Product Management informed about execution and raise risks accordingly that could affect the release schedule, quality, or feature-set.
Manage the release's dependency chains: e.g. compiler features that libraries depend on, interfaces shared between the SDK and the runtime, LLVM and toolchain versions, board and silicon availability, etc.

Maintain Release Quality

Establish with our teams release quality gates: e.g. no regressions in cycles, energy, or code size on the benchmark suites relative to the previous release; test coverage thresholds met, etc.

Run the release checklist (the gates above plus documentation, release notes, etc.), working with the release shepherd to hold owners to closure criteria.

Track escaped defects and feed what we learn back into the checklist.

Manage Risk, Decisions, and Reporting

Surface risk early with mitigation options and schedule impact quantified: e.g. late compiler features, coverage shortfalls, and benchmark regressions.
Facilitate scope, schedule, and quality tradeoffs, and document what was decided, by whom, and why.
Deliver executive reporting: where the release stands, what is at risk, what decision is needed and by when.

Required Qualifications

B.S. in Electrical/Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent; M.S. or MBA a plus.
7+ years in software engineering or program management, including prior hands-on engineering experience in compilers, systems software, or embedded software.
Working fluency in using AI-tools to facilitate program management – from reporting, to issue tracking, to dependency analysis and more.
Strong experience with the software delivery flow: compiler toolchains, embedded SDKs, CI/CD, test coverage, performance benchmarking, and release engineering.
Demonstrated ability to build and defend a bottoms-up schedule with critical path analysis and dependency mapping.
Track record influencing without authority: earning the technical credibility to push senior engineers on commitments and dates.
Strong written and verbal communication; able to run a room of principal engineers and an executive review with equal effectiveness.
Hands-on with program tooling: Github, Linear, Jira, Notion, Confluence, CI systems, etc.

Desired Qualifications & Experience Requirements

Experience as the technical program manager on a first-generation silicon product, where the toolchain and hardware matured together.
Familiarity with LLVM or MLIR, machine learning compilers, or language runtimes.
Knowledge of dataflow, spatial, or other novel compute architectures.
Experience managing pre-silicon software enablement against emulation or FPGA prototyping programs.

We offer a competitive base salary for this role, generally ranging from $200,000 to $260,000, plus a 10% annual bonus, meaningful equity, and comprehensive benefits. Final compensation will depend on experience, level, and location, with flexibility for the right candidate.

Why Join Efficient?

Build what's next. At Efficient, you'll tackle big challenges with room to take ownership and make an impact. We back you with competitive pay, equity, a 401(k) match, company-paid benefits, paid parental leave, and flexibility—plus opportunities to grow your skills and career as we scale.

new_jobs.description:
Everpure (NYSE: P) has evolved from storage pioneer to data platform, closing fiscal 2026 with $3.7 billion in revenue, its first billion-dollar quarter, and accelerating growth into FY27. Our strategic agenda spans the companies defining the next era of technology - hyperscalers, AI labs, the AI hardware supply chain, data platform providers, and the broader AI ecosystem.

This type of work—work that changes the world—is what the tech industry was founded on. So, if you're ready to seize the endless opportunities and leave your mark, come join us.

THE ROLE

Everpure's global contract manufacturing network needs a single owner for capacity governance and supply chain network resilience — someone who replaces fragmented, reactive decision-making with one coherent framework spanning all lines of business. This role sits at the center of that shift: building the governance structures, risk frameworks, and executive reporting that let the network absorb shocks — geopolitical, infrastructure, business continuity — without derailing growth targets. You'll work closely with the Network Design Council, site managers, CM partners, and cross-functional teams like Mfg Product & Test Engineering, R&D Engineering, and Indirect Sourcing, with real influence over how capacity and risk decisions get made across the network.

What You'll Do

Own and govern the Global Capacity Planning Framework, building the RACI that gives the Supply Chain Network Council one source of truth across all lines of business
Serve as the central escalation point for capacity issues network-wide, running a Monthly Global Capacity Review and standardized dashboards that keep site managers and CM partners aligned
Define and govern Time to Recover (TTR) and Time to Survive/Time to Fail (TTF) resilience KPIs across all global production sites and products, translating gaps into prioritized mitigation plans for the highest-risk sites
Drive the Capacity Analysis Tool and executive Tableau dashboard roadmap, and own the capital budget that funds capacity and resilience investments against growth targets
Partner with Indirect Sourcing and Engineering to optimize test process & time, landed cost through data research, common infrastructure parts and improved CM pricing and forecasting

What You Bring

Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Hardware Engineering, Operations Research, Supply Chain, or related field; Master’s degree preferred. Six Sigma Green Belt certification or above preferred.

Proven ability to lead complex, technically-oriented transformation projects, utilizing methodologies like Waterfall, Agile, or Scrum to manage scope, schedules, and deliverables in a dynamic environment, paired with exceptional communication and negotiation skills to translate technical/data concepts for non-technical stakeholders and build consensus across supply chain, IT, and engineering teams.
Deep fluency in global contract manufacturing capacity planning, built through experience designing governance frameworks, RACIs, and executive review cadences that hold up across a complex, matrixed network
Strong analytical capability — comfortable building capacity models and KPI dashboards in tools like Tableau, and partnering with BI/analytics teams on executive-facing reporting
Experience building supply chain risk and resilience programs, including business continuity planning, scenario analysis, and recovery metrics such as Time to Recover and Time to Survive/Fail
Skilled at driving alignment across cross-functional, matrixed teams without direct authority — able to influence site managers, CM partners, and senior stakeholders toward a shared framework
We are primarily an in-office environment and therefore, you will be expected to work from the Santa Clara, CA office in compliance with Everpure's policies, unless you are on PTO, or work travel, or other approved leave.

Description

Northland Controls is seeking an experienced Embedded Program Manager in Sunnyvale, CA. This is an exciting opportunity for a proven security industry professional who enjoys working closely with enterprise customers, leading global service programs, developing high-performing teams, and continuously improving service delivery.

In this role, you will be embedded within a key enterprise customer account, serving as a trusted program partner and primary point of coordination between the customer and Northland Controls. You will lead a multidisciplinary embedded team that may include Project Managers, consultants, systems technicians, and engineers, ensuring services are delivered in accordance with program requirements and customer priorities.

You will maintain regular touch points with the global team, review and verify work, provide monthly program updates, partner with customer leadership on challenges and opportunities, and lead quarterly business reviews focused on KPIs, SLAs, priorities, and continuous improvement. You will also be accountable for the performance and development of each team member and for making resource or team adjustments when delivery expectations are not being met.

If you're looking for an opportunity to become deeply integrated with a global customer program, strengthen service delivery, develop talented teams, and make a measurable impact in a growing organization, we'd love to hear from you.

What You'll Do

Serve as the embedded program leader within a key enterprise customer account, developing a strong understanding of the customer's organization, security program, priorities, standards, operating model, and long-term objectives.
Maintain daily or regular touch points with the global embedded team to review priorities, verify work, remove blockers, and ensure services are being delivered in accordance with program requirements.
Act as the primary point of contact between the customer and Northland Controls for program-level planning, performance, communication, escalation, and issue resolution.
Partner closely with customer management on strategic focus areas, active projects, delivery improvements, program challenges, opportunities, and the ongoing evolution of the program.
Lead, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary team that may include Project Managers, consultants, systems technicians, and engineers, fostering a collaborative and high-performing work environment.
Establish clear expectations for each team member and hold individuals accountable for performance, service quality, responsiveness, and delivery commitments.
Provide ongoing coaching, feedback, mentorship, and direction; manage performance improvement and corrective action in accordance with Northland processes, and recommend team adjustments when sustained improvement is not achieved.
Allocate and prioritize resources across projects, operational needs, and customer initiatives while balancing workloads and optimizing utilization, productivity, and coverage.
Track program performance using KPIs, SLAs, delivery milestones, workload data, and other relevant metrics; identify trends and take action when performance is at risk.
Prepare and deliver regular program updates to customer stakeholders and Northland leadership, including performance, resource, financial, risk, and improvement reporting.
Lead the development and presentation of Quarterly Business Reviews, coordinating team inputs, reporting against KPIs and SLAs, collecting customer feedback, aligning on quarterly priorities, and driving follow-through on agreed actions.
Build and maintain trusted relationships with customer stakeholders, proactively managing expectations, addressing concerns, and supporting strong satisfaction and confidence in the team's services.
Track and analyze relationship and service indicators, including stakeholder feedback, responsiveness, recurring concerns, and service-quality trends, to assess the effectiveness of program delivery and relationship management.
Identify program risks, dependencies, and issues; develop mitigation plans and work with customer management and Northland leadership to proactively address challenges and keep delivery on track.
Manage the overall embedded team budget, monitor expenditures and forecasts, identify budget risks, and provide monthly financial and accrual reporting as required.
Conduct regular quality reviews of team outputs and service delivery to ensure work aligns with customer requirements, established standards, and program expectations.
Drive continuous improvement by analyzing scheduling, workload, performance, and service data to identify inefficiencies, bottlenecks, and opportunities to improve delivery processes and outcomes.
Coordinate across internal teams, customer stakeholders, program peers, suppliers, and dependency partners to align delivery, share best practices, and ensure seamless integration of work across the program.
Gather and analyze feedback from customer stakeholders and team members and translate that feedback into practical improvements to services, processes, team performance, and working relationships.
Proactively identify and resolve conflicts, facilitating practical solutions and timely escalation when issues require additional leadership involvement.
Conduct periodic program evaluations and lessons-learned reviews to assess outcomes, document improvements, and inform future program planning and service strategy.
Travel to customer locations and team sites as required.

What We're Looking For

Significant experience managing complex enterprise programs, embedded services, or technical service-delivery teams within the security industry or a closely related technical environment.
Proven experience working directly with enterprise customers and managing long-term customer relationships in a high-visibility, service-oriented environment.
Proven experience leading, coaching, and developing multidisciplinary teams, including direct accountability for individual performance and service delivery.
Strong experience with KPI and SLA management, executive-level program reporting, Quarterly Business Reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Strong understanding of program financial management, budgeting, forecasting, accrual reporting, resource planning, workload balancing, and cost controls.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, stakeholders, dependencies, and competing requirements within a large global customer environment.
Strong knowledge of physical security systems and services, including access control, video surveillance, and related enterprise technologies.
Experience with Lenel, Software House, or similar enterprise security platforms; relevant certifications are highly desirable.
PMP certification or equivalent program or project management credentials preferred.
Excellent leadership, communication, presentation, facilitation, and organizational skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with both technical teams and senior customer stakeholders.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify trends, anticipate risks, navigate changing priorities, and drive issues through resolution.
Ability to build productive, trusted relationships with customers, colleagues, suppliers, and business partners while operating effectively as both a customer-facing partner and a representative of Northland Controls.
Valid driver's license and ability to travel as required.

Why Join Northland Controls?

At Northland Controls, you'll have the opportunity to become an integral part of a key enterprise customer's global security program while leading the people, processes, and performance that support consistent service delivery. You'll work alongside experienced customer, project, engineering, and operations professionals while helping strengthen the teams and operating practices that support our continued growth.

We value innovation, accountability, collaboration, and doing what it takes to deliver exceptional results for our customers. As an Embedded Program Manager, you'll have the opportunity to build lasting customer partnerships, develop your team, improve how services are delivered, and make a meaningful impact across the organization.

Northland Controls offers competitive compensation, comprehensive health and retirement benefits, professional development opportunities, and a flexible working environment.

new_jobs.description:
Company Description

At Henry Ford Health, we're committed to advancing health and improving lives for the millions of people we serve across Michigan and around the world. As one of the nation's leading academic health systems, we provide a comprehensive continuum of care that includes primary and preventive services, specialty and complex care, virtual care, pharmacy, home health, eye care, health insurance, and more. With 12 hospitals and hundreds of ambulatory care locations, including former Ascension Southeast Michigan and Flint Region facilities, our growing network expands access to exceptional care in the communities we serve.

Headquartered in Detroit, Henry Ford Health is helping shape the future of healthcare through the transformative Future of Health: Detroit initiative, a $3 billion investment that is redefining our academic healthcare campus and advancing innovation, research, education, and community impact.

Our work is grounded in purpose, collaboration, and belonging. We empower team members to grow their careers, contribute innovative ideas, and make a meaningful difference every day. Whether you're caring for patients, supporting operations, conducting research, or driving new solutions, you'll be part of a team united by a shared mission: delivering exceptional care, advancing health outcomes, and building healthier communities for all.

Job Description

GENERAL SUMMARY:

As a Community Health Worker (CHW), you'll be a trusted bridge between healthcare, social services, and the communities we serve—making a real difference in people's lives every day. Under the leadership of the Office of Community Health, Equity & Wellness' CHW Hub Manager, and in partnership with designated onsite leaders, you'll serve as a vital liaison who promotes access to healthcare services, improves health and equity outcomes, and helps patients navigate the systems that support their wellbeing. Whether integrated directly within a clinical care team or assigned to a specific project, you'll play a critical role in addressing social determinants of health (SDOH), connecting individuals to essential services, and delivering patient-centered, culturally relevant care that truly matters.

Principal Duties And Responsibilities

Identify and address patients' non-medical and social determinant of health needs—including food security, housing, transportation, and social support—by providing meaningful referrals to appropriate social service agencies and tracking positive outcomes.
Collaborate with clinical care teams to ensure seamless continuity of care, co-develop personalized care plans, and provide compassionate follow-up support through home visits and telephonic check-ins that strengthen patient relationships.
Drive patient engagement and retention by conducting direct outreach that improves recruitment, supports adherence to care instructions, and increases utilization of primary and preventive care services—ultimately reducing no-show rates and unnecessary emergency department visits.
Build trust and foster community connections through authentic outreach that helps bridge healthcare services with the communities we serve.
Empower patients through culturally competent health education and coaching—delivered individually and in group settings—that focuses on disease prevention, health promotion, and effective chronic disease management.
Advocate for patients by identifying and removing barriers to care (such as insurance enrollment, transportation, housing, and language access), facilitating connections to resources, and supporting individuals in confidently navigating both healthcare and social service systems.
